cases.scenario: A change implements a handler behind an already agreed local route while request and response semantics remain unchanged.
cases.rationale: The material consequence stays within the assigned implementation surface; prescribing exact local HOW would be over-governance.

cases.scenario: A change alters a published route's request, response, or compatibility behavior.
cases.rationale: The change affects an externally meaningful contract, so Executor must escalate for Architect authority or revision.

cases.scenario: A change reorganizes SQL statements or local query helpers without changing stored data, transaction, or consistency semantics.
cases.rationale: The change is mechanical within the existing persistence behavior; imposing Architect control over local organization would be over-governance.

cases.scenario: A change alters stored data shape, transaction boundaries, retention, or consistency behavior.
cases.rationale: Persistence semantics have material data and recovery consequences that require Architect authority or revision.

cases.scenario: A new internal helper or module stays owned and consumed within one existing component.
cases.rationale: Ownership remains inside the existing component, so choosing the local implementation shape is Executor judgment.

cases.scenario: A new reusable helper crosses component boundaries and creates a shared ownership contract.
cases.rationale: Cross-component reuse creates a new ownership boundary and contract, which requires Architect authority or revision.

cases.scenario: An implementation uses a dependency already approved by the task without changing its runtime or cost assumptions.
cases.rationale: The dependency consequence is already authorized and unchanged; re-prescribing the local use would be over-governance.

cases.scenario: An implementation introduces a dependency whose footprint, runtime, license, cost, or deployment topology changes project consequences.
cases.rationale: A materially new dependency changes project cost or topology, so Executor must escalate for authority or a revised contract.

cases.scenario: A generated or companion file is updated as local mechanics while its externally observed contract stays unchanged.
cases.rationale: The generated change remains local mechanics with no external contract consequence; prescribing its exact form would be over-governance.

cases.scenario: A generated artifact or companion file changes an externally consumed schema, API, or compatibility contract.
cases.rationale: The generated output changes an externally meaningful contract and therefore requires Architect authority or revision.

cases.scenario: An implementation follows already frozen authentication or authorization behavior without changing who is trusted or what is reachable.
cases.rationale: The implementation preserves the frozen trust boundary, so local execution judgment remains sufficient.

cases.scenario: An implementation changes credential interpretation, trust relationships, authorization reachability, or the security boundary.
cases.rationale: Changing the trust boundary is a material security and authority consequence that requires Architect authority or revision.

cases.scenario: Two local implementations satisfy the same authorized behavior and preserve all material consequences; choosing between them is a preference-only HOW decision.
cases.rationale: No material consequence changes, so an Architect prescription or revision based only on preferred wording or local HOW would be over-governance.

cases.scenario: A proposed local HOW changes reliability, data exposure, public behavior, ownership, cost, or reversibility even though the requested feature sounds similar.
cases.rationale: The apparently local HOW carries a material consequence, so proceeding without Architect authority or revision would be under-governance.

cases.scenario: Unexpected companion work remains local to the same component and preserves its external behavior and ownership.
cases.rationale: The companion work preserves the existing boundary and consequence, so local Executor judgment remains appropriate.

cases.scenario: Unexpected companion work moves behavior or ownership across components and creates a new cross-component contract.
cases.rationale: Moving ownership across components creates a material contract and architecture consequence that requires Architect authority or revision.
